concept_title: 보랏빛 달밤의 매화 무대, 뱀과 렌
revision_note: V1 (2ac3ad0) rejected by the owner: too many borders. V2 (73a2823) merged the sky, both lattice doors and the moon/cloud layer into one back plate, shrank the clear rim 2.5 -> 1.0 mm and rendered clear acrylic see-through in the assembly preview. V3 (657a484) recomposed the scene but the owner prefers V2 ("v2가 낫다고 한거야"). V4 (a2a83cd) = V2 plus two owner requests: the blossom tree printed diagonally into the back panel and Len "seated" by cropping her raster at the seat line. V5 (7459c7f) restructured the scene (Len whole on a 70 mm serpent's coil, the tree back as ONE cut plate whose 2.5 mm canopy envelope webbed the blossoms together with clear acrylic) and the owner rejected it ("이거 아니야 v4에서 잘림 문제만 해결하고 나무를 예시 이미지처럼 대각선 배치 해달라고"). V6 (62963a8) = V4 with exactly those two changes: Len shown whole on the base line and the tree printed into the back panel, leaning up to the right like the concept. V7 = the owner's decision on the tree ("벚꽃하고 나무는 별도 에셋으로 분리해줘"): the tree is no longer printed on the back panel and is no longer one clear-webbed piece. 03_blossom_tree.png is split by colour into (a) a TREE cut piece = the dark trunk and branches (wood pixels; twigs thinner than 0.5 mm pruned so every feature is at least 2.5 mm after the 1.0 mm rim) standing on its own tab on its own depth row (31) with its base behind the serpent, and (b) six BLOSSOM cut pieces = pink petal clusters grouped around branch tips (5 mm sky gaps between clusters), each a separate plate with a 1.0 mm rim, no clear webbing between clusters, mounted on the base BEHIND the tree plate on two depth rows (39 and 47) on a 12.25 mm clear stem so the branches cross in front of them and the gaps between clusters show the sky and moon like the concept. Everything else is V6 exactly: whole seated Len, serpent, moon, doors, base, layout, rims.

finished_size_mm.note: 3T: base 3 + back panel 90 art + 1.0 mm rim = 94; the tallest blossom plate (upper-centre cluster, apex z 88 + 1.0 rim + 2.6 tab) assembles to 91.6 mm above the base top and stays under the back panel.

clear_border_rationale: docs/laser-cut-quality.md fixes no rim minimum; its hard limits are the 0.035 mm curve deviation and the 12 mm load-path floor on the buffered silhouette. 1.0 mm is the smallest round offset that still keeps UV ink 0.5 mm inside the cut edge under a 0.5 mm print registration error. V7 keeps 1.0 mm on every plate including the new tree and blossom pieces ("no fat rims - 1.0 mm"); the only local widening is a 0.6 mm closing applied after the rim so that two branches closer than 2 mm end up joined by at least a 1.2 mm clear bridge instead of a zero-width pinch (measured minimum art-to-cut stays 0.985 mm).

V6 owner request (fix the cropping): the whole 84 mm figure at V4's scale, x and row - no crop_below_fraction. Her long leg's boot sole is the lowest ink, so both boot rims rest on the base line 1.0 mm (rim) above the base top, the sword tip 3 mm above it and the hips (crotch line) 33 mm above it; the pose (one leg hanging to the base, one knee raised, sword down-left) reads as seated on the base edge. The tab under the art centre sits between the two boots where the buffered silhouette is narrower than the 12 mm load-path floor, so the bud guard raises a 12.25 mm clear riser inside the tab window from the base line up to where the legs close (about 9 mm); it is the only clear support and carries no print.

front_view_policy.note: ORIGIN is a deliberately stacked centre scene (blossom plates behind the tree plate, tree behind the serpent and character): polygon occlusion is by design and overstates visual blocking. Numbers are recorded per piece in validation_report.json; composition acceptance is the vision-checked assembly preview against the supplied concept art. Structural checks (row clearance, overhang, load path, gaps, rims, minimum feature) stay hard.

tree_split.scale_note: 88 mm art (unrotated alpha box 1283 x 990 px = 285 ppi at this size, embedded at native pixels) so the whole rotated tree (105.7 x 88.4 mm) stands on the base line inside the 90 mm sky: the treetop reaches z 89.4, under the back panel top (91). V6 printed a 100 mm tree with its lowest 18.4 mm clipped off by the sky rectangle; a physical plate cannot be clipped, so the tree is scaled to fit whole.
tree_split.colour_rule: opaque = alpha > 128; petal = r - max(g, b) >= 45 and r >= 110 (pink/magenta petals); wood = every other opaque pixel (dark trunk, branches, mauve highlights). Pixels are classified on the native-resolution 35 deg clockwise rotation that V6 already used (premultiplied alpha, cubic).
tree_split.wood_rule: wood mask closed 0.3 mm (anti-aliasing gaps), opened 0.5 mm (minimum feature: twigs thinner than 0.5 mm of ink are pruned so no cut feature is below 2.5 mm after the rim), largest connected component kept; the cut silhouette is its contour smoothed along the contour (sigma 2.5 px = 0.22 mm, so the pixel staircase cannot trip the segment gate), buffered 1.0 mm and closed 0.6 mm. The print is the original pixels inside the kept skeleton mask.
tree_split.cluster_rule: petal mask closed/opened 0.3 mm; each cluster = petals inside its seed disc (Voronoi among seeds) that lie at least 2.5 mm (half the 5 mm cluster gap) away from every other seed's cell, closed 0.6 mm so touching flowers join, largest component kept, islands dropped; cut = outer contour (enclosed holes filled clear) smoothed, buffered 1.0 mm, closed 0.6 mm. Print = every original opaque pixel inside that contour (petals plus the twigs between them). Petals outside the discs or inside the 5 mm gaps are not cut, so neighbouring plates show at least 2 mm of sky.
tree_split.stem_rule: each blossom plate stands on the base on a clear unprinted stem 12.25 mm wide (the load-path riser width) under its 18 mm tab; the stem top sits 2 mm inside the cluster so the join is inside the rim.
tree_split.min_feature_rule: after the rim every neck of every new piece must measure at least 2.5 mm (erosion test), the rim 1.0 mm +/- 0.02, the stem 12.25 mm >= the 12 mm load-path floor; every cluster must pass laser_paths.audit_path (segments <= max(100, 1.5 x perimeter mm)).
tree_split.dropped_petals: the lower-right lobe (image x 55-95, y 55-96 mm = scene x 152-192, z 0-34) sits behind Len's legs at the base line; the small centre-lower-left cluster (scene x 135-153, z 41-59, about 75 mm2 of ink) sits behind the trunk fork and is not cut either; petals inside the 5 mm gaps between clusters are not cut. The sky and moon show through those gaps.
tree_split.rows_note: tree row 31 (8 mm behind the serpent row 23, so 5T slots keep a 3 mm gap); blossom rows 39 and 47 (8 and 16 mm behind the tree plane, 9 mm in front of the back panel slots). Two rows suffice once neighbouring clusters keep a 5 mm sky gap: the only front-view overlaps left are stems passing behind another cluster (upper-centre behind left-middle, upper-centre-right behind centre-right-lower, upper-left behind left-middle), and in each of them the crossed cluster sits on the nearer row so no clear stem shows in front of a pink cluster. Same-row blossom tabs are at least 22 mm apart and their standing cuts at least 2 mm apart; every slot is at least 2.99 mm from every other slot at both thicknesses.

board_layout_note: Product master board 340 x 420 mm: back panel top-left, character lower-left, serpent right, tree right-centre, the seven blossom plates in two rows between the character and the serpent; the A3 stage re-nests the same cut polygons at a 3 mm gap.
